title: Tenant Connectivity Compatibility Matrix and Terraform Deprecation Roadmap (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a practical reference and tactical roadmap for:
- Enumerating tenant connectivity surface area (connectors, NAT/egress patterns, sidecars, peering).
- A compatibility matrix that maps current customer topologies to recommended Terraform module versions and upgrade paths.
- A deprecation schedule for older TF module variants (v1.*), and automation guidance for 0->1 migrations.

Scope:
- Private deployments (VPC + on-prem hybrid) only.
- Focus on networking primitives that block safe upgrades: BGP peering configs, NAT gateways vs egress-proxy, subnet tagging, CNI choices, and customer proxy patterns.
- Does NOT cover app-level auth, KMS/HSM rotation, or tenant data model migrations (separate playbooks).

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- We will formally deprecate terraform-modules/network:v1.x for new tenant activations after 2026-05-01.
- Provide automated migration path using a two-phase apply: (1) side-by-side modules + canary tenant; (2) staged cutover with traffic drain.
- Key compatibility hits: legacy egressless proxies (customers using iptables NAT hack) and non-standard CNI will require manual adaptation.

Compatibility matrix (human-readable):
Columns: Connector pattern | Customer environment | TF module required | Risk level | Notes
- Transit-gateway-peering | AWS multi-account, TGW hub-spoke | network:v2.1+ | medium | v2.1 adds route table tagging to preserve TGW associations; requires az-aware subnets.
- Shared-nat-gateway | Single-account high-throughput | network:v2.0+ | low | can use bursting autoscale NATs; v2.0 exposes nat pool sizing var.
- Egress-proxy (squid corporate) | On-prem -> cloud via IPsec | network:onprem-bridge:v1.4 | high | onprem-bridge v1.4 implements proxy-aware healthchecks; recommends sticky routes.
- Private-link-only | Strict egress blocked | network:v2.2+ | medium-high | v2.2 supports endpoint services and per-tenant identity mapping.
- Cilium/CNI-legacy | Non-standard CNI with custom MTU | network:custom-cni-adapter:v1 | high | manual review; we do not have automated migration for kernel-space CNIs.

Upgrade / deprecation roadmap (high level):
1) Announcement phase (now -> 2026-03-31)
   - Notify account teams + CS playbook, post Confluence announcement with migration checklist.
   - Publish compatibility matrix (this doc).
2) Migration tools & canary (2026-04-01 -> 2026-05-15)
   - Merge TF helper scripts PR (linked).
   - Run canary migration for 3 internal tenants in staging.
3) Soft-deprecation (2026-05-16 -> 2026-07-31)
   - New tenants blocked from defaulting to v1 modules (CI/CD check).
   - Existing tenants can opt-in; we provide free migration runbooks for Enterprise customers.
4) Full deprecation (after 2026-08-01)
   - Remove v1 modules from documented golden path; mark as EOL.

Step-by-step migration pattern (recommended):
- Phase A: Preflight (automated + manual checks)
  * run: ./scripts/tf-preflight --target-tenant=<id>  # collects current TF state, lists incompatible constructs
  * verify: no custom kernel CNIs, no iptables NAT hacks, public-eips < quota threshold
  * backup: snapshot TF state, export provider state to secure bucket (encrypted)
- Phase B: Side-by-side apply
  * deploy newer module namespace using module.namespace = "rwinf-tenant-<id>-v2" (non-destructive resources only)
  * validate connectivity with isolated traffic tests (See test-plan below)
- Phase C: Cutover
  * perform route table swaps or update TGW attachments as appropriate during low-traffic window
  * drain connection using TCP timeout/sessions drain scripts (example included)
- Phase D: Cleanup + certs rotation
  * remove old module resources, rotate ephemeral credentials, update runbooks

Preflight checklist (automatable):
- [ ] TF state export succeeded and uploaded to s3://rwinf-tf-backups/<tenant>/<timestamp>
- [ ] Customer security team confirmed proxy/egress patterns are supported
- [ ] Verify IP address availability in target subnet (>= 20% slack)
- [ ] Confirm PKI paths for endpoint services are valid (no mismatched CNs)
- [ ] Confirm SRE runbook on-call availability (2 people)

Rollback strategy (fast-fail safe):
- If post-cutover validation fails (connectivity or latency regressions >10% SLI):
  * Step 1: Re-attach previous route tables / restore TGW association from snapshot
  * Step 2: Re-instate previous NAT gateway pair (we keep them for 24 hours)
  * Step 3: Trigger emergency terraform apply using previous statefile and mark tenant as roll-backed in JIRA ticket

Testing plan (automation):
- Integration smoke tests: 1) DNS resolution through customer resolver, 2) HTTPs egress via corporate proxy, 3) Long-lived websocket stability for 30 minutes.
- Performance tests: synthetic token-per-second load through inference gateway (target baseline + 20%).
- Security tests: IP spoofing, port scan (low intensity), endpoint service ACL validation.
- Test harness: use infra/test-harness/tenant-network-sim (docker compose) for quick local reproduction.

Terraform notes (practical tips):
- Use workspace per-tenant pattern (do not share root workspace).
- Example migration command sequence (simplified):
  * terraform init -upgrade 
  * terraform workspace select tenant-123 || terraform workspace new tenant-123
  * terraform plan -var-file=tenant-123.tfvars -out=plan-v2.tfplan
  * terraform apply plan-v2.tfplan  # side-by-side apply uses module.namespace to prevent name collision
- Module version pinning: prefer = "~> 2.0.0" for minor stability, avoid ">=" pins that cause surprise upgrades
- Keep a regeneration script for CRL/PKI in tools/rotate-keys.sh (items our onprem customers need)

Operational signals and success criteria (for canary->general rollout):
- Connection success rate >= 99.5% over 24h for control-plane ops
- Token-per-second throughput within 10% of baseline during steady-state tests
- No critical incidents in 7 days post-cutover for canary tenants

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self + follow-ups):
- [ ] Confirm legal/regulatory requirements for on-prem air-gapped tenants (liaise with security/compliance).
- [ ] Decide on automated EMR for customers with heavy outbound TLS inspection (Marco to prototype).
- [ ] Add small diagram showing TGW route table swap sequence (ask design for simple sketch).
- [ ] Finalize deprecation announcement language with comms (Asha).

Unresolved technical risks:
- Stateful middleboxes: any customer NAT hairpinning or DPI device that relies on ephemeral source IPs will likely break; these need manual runbooks.
- CNI kernel hooks: if packet manipulation occurs in kernel (e.g., TC rules), migration cannot be automated.

Appendix: example customer migration notes (free-form)
- Tenant: AcmeCorp (onprem + aws hybrid)
  * Observed: uses squid proxy for egress, custom route-table naming, CNI: calico old kernel mode
  * Recommendation: migrate proxy to egress-proxy module + schedule maintenance window for kernel upgrade; manual action required for calico kernel mode.
  * Estimated effort: 4 dev-days + 2 infra-days (on-prem access needed).

Contact/owners: Lina Chen (owner), Marco Diaz (migration tooling), Asha Patel (CS comms), SRE on-call for private-deployments

Notes on doc hygiene: save updates under new filename incremental changes (date) to keep audit trail. This is intentionally a working doc — expect fragmented checklists and early drafts.
